item.title: CVE-2026-131582 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.2
item.description: Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.2 | The PagBank / PagSeguro e Vindi para WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'customer.name' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.1.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload can be planted via the legitimate hosted-checkout (Checkout PB) flow simply by entering it as a customer name on PagBank's payment page, requiring no hash brute-forcing whatsoever; the woocommerce_api_rm_ps_notif webhook path is additionally exploitable because its only gate is a 5-character (20-bit) truncated wp_hash() that is trivially brute-forceable.

item.title: CVE-2026-131587 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3
item.description: Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3 | The Recipe Card Blocks Lite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 4.0.2 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to overwrite the post_content of arbitrary posts on the site, including Administrator-owned published posts, bypassing the edit_others_posts and edit_published_posts capability checks. This vulnerability is only exploitable when the wpzoom_rcb_settings_synchronize_recipe_post setting is enabled, and requires the target post to contain at least one Recipe Card block whose twin can be matched to the attacker's draft recipe post.

item.description: Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.4 | The Mail Mint – Email Marketing, Automation & WooCommerce Emails with AI Assistance plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'form_id' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.31.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. item.title: CVE-2026-133421 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9 | Validating an untrusted ISO 8601 duration string into a timedelta field with Pydantic V1 takes quadratic time: an input of a few dozen kilobytes takes seconds to validate.
The iso8601_duration_re regular expression used to parse ISO 8601 durations (in pydantic/datetime_parse.py) contains an unescaped ".", which also matches digits. On a string of digits, the repeated groups overlap and the regex engine backtracks in quadratic time.
The issue was fixed in commit 62791e66a9f8f118e465ed760c9e2ede9ae3055e. Users relying on the pydantic.v1 namespace in Pydantic V2 should upgrade to 2.14.2 or later.
Impact: denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted strings into timedelta fields.

item.title: CVE-2026-133422 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9 | Validating an untrusted list into a field constrained with unique_items=True with Pydantic V1 takes quadratic time: an input of a few hundred kilobytes takes seconds to validate.
The ConstrainedList.unique_items_validator validator (in pydantic/types.py) checks each item against all the following ones. For a list with no duplicates (the common, valid case), this results in a quadratic number of comparisons.
The issue was fixed in commit 6ec75e57f277a820ec583e601167f25fe8dc7c87. Users relying on the pydantic.v1 namespace in Pydantic V2 should upgrade to 2.14.2 or later.
Impact: denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted lists into fields constrained with unique_items=True (using conlist() or Field()).
The fix only applies to lists of builtin scalar types (int, float, str, bytes, bool and None), for which duplicates can be detected in linear time. Lists of other types (e.g. models or dictionaries) are still checked in quadratic time, as their items aren't guaranteed to be hashable: bound their size using the max_items constraint.
Pydantic V2 models are not affected.

item.title: CVE-2026-133424 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | When extra data is allowed, providing both the alias and the name of an aliased TypedDict or dataclass field makes the unvalidated value (provided under the name) overwrite the validated one (provided under the alias), resulting in validated data not matching the declared type.
Extra items are stored in the same dictionary as the fields (the returned dictionary for TypedDict, the instance __dict__ for dataclasses). As only the alias is marked as used, the field name is treated as an extra item, and its unvalidated value overrides the validated one. The TypedDict validator (pydantic-core/src/validators/typed_dict.rs) and the dataclass validator (pydantic-core/src/validators/dataclass.rs) share this logic.
The issue was fixed in commit 34491f5328f168f14e3769cd5f0f83c0af0f4778.
Impact: validation bypass, as data returned by validation doesn't match the declared type. Affected are applications validating untrusted data into TypedDict or dataclass types with aliased fields and extra data allowed (with extra='allow', or with the extra_items argument for TypedDict), using Pydantic V2 (up to and including 2.14.1).
Pydantic models (BaseModel) are not affected, as extra data is stored separately from fields.

item.title: CVE-2026-133426 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | Validating an untrusted string in exponent notation into a Fraction field computes the full power of ten without any bound: an input of a few bytes takes seconds to validate.
String inputs are passed to the Fraction constructor. For strings in exponent notation (e.g. '1e8000000'), CPython computes the corresponding power of ten as an integer (in Lib/fractions.py).
The issue was fixed in commit 69ed168e9ad465eef4c8d81efb152a93b604daf5. For strings in exponent notation, the exponent is now parsed before calling the Fraction constructor, and exponents larger than 4300 (in absolute value) are rejected.
Impact: denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted strings into Fraction fields (in both JSON and Python mode, including in strict mode), using Pydantic from 2.10.0 up to (but excluding) 2.14.0.
From 2.14.0, exponents larger than 4300 (in absolute value) are rejected, matching the maximum number of digits accepted for integers.

item.title: CVE-2026-133428 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | Validating an untrusted URL with a long scheme and many hosts into a multi-host URL field (e.g. PostgresDsn) takes quadratic time and memory: an input of about a hundred kilobytes takes around a gigabyte of memory to validate.
The parse_multihost_url() function (in pydantic-core/src/validators/url.rs) parses each host separately, prepending the whole URL prefix (including the scheme) to every one of them. As the scheme can be arbitrarily long, and is parsed and stored once per host, both time and memory grow quadratically with the input size. Allowed schemes (e.g. postgres for PostgresDsn) are only checked after parsing, so they don't prevent the issue.
The issue was fixed in commit b4028f9d87e34750e53be0ba011d70f3c0fcc94e.
Impact: denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted strings into multi-host URL fields (PostgresDsn, MongoDsn, NatsDsn, or custom types built on MultiHostUrl).

Affected are applications validating untrusted JSON data into models allowing extra data (with extra='allow'), with a key type annotated on __pydantic_extra__ (e.g. dict[Annotated[str, Field(pattern=...)], int]), using Pydantic from 2.13.0 up to (but excluding) 2.14.2.

item.title: CVE-2026-133505 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 5.9

item.title: CVE-2026-133611 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 4.6
item.description: Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 4.6 | vulnerability-lookup prior to version 7.1.0 contains two security issues in its web interface. First, the /user/toggle_2fa endpoint accepted HTTP GET requests and disabled the authenticated user's two-factor authentication without requiring password confirmation. Because the state-changing operation was reachable via GET, an attacker with a basic account could embed an image element (or any other GET-triggering markup) in a comment pointing to that endpoint. When a victim with 2FA enabled viewed the comment, their browser silently issued the GET request, disabling the victim's second factor of authentication. No CSRF token was enforced on the GET path, and no password was required to confirm the action. Second, the comment detail page (/comment/<uuid>) rendered unpublished comments to any visitor who possessed the URL, bypassing the moderation workflow that was intended to keep such content hidden until approved. The API correctly restricted access, but the web view did not enforce the same authorization check. The combined effect allows an attacker to degrade a victim's account security (removal of 2FA) through a single page view and to read content that was not yet approved for public release.

item.title: CVE-2026-133613 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.4
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.4 | Flowintel's community data launcher script passes the admin API key as a command-line argument to a child Python helper process. On Unix-like systems, process arguments are readable by all local users via standard tools such as ps or by reading /proc/<pid>/cmdline, allowing any local user to observe the key while the helper process is running.
An attacker with local access to the host can capture the admin API key during the brief window in which the helper process is active. Possession of the key grants full administrative access to the Flowintel REST API, enabling unauthorized creation, modification, or deletion of threat intelligence data, users, roles, and organisations.
Preconditions: - The victim must invoke the community data import or deletion command (launch.sh -tdc or -dtdc) with the API key supplied as a positional argument. - The attacker must have a local user account on the same host and be able to observe process listings during the helper execution window.

item.title: CVE-2026-99796 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
io_uring/poll: cancel all matching requests in one pass
With IORING_ASYNC_CANCEL_ALL, __io_async_cancel() calls io_try_cancel() until nothing is found, and io_poll_cancel() cancels one request per call, starting each lookup at the beginning of the hash. A cancelled request stays hashed until its task work runs, so every lookup walks past the ones already cancelled. Cancelling K of N pending polls visits about K*N/2 requests in one io_uring_enter(), with uring_lock held.
A single CANCEL_FD|ALL on 80000 polls on one eventfd takes 17.06s, 0.02s with this change. With voluntary preemption the soft lockup watchdog fires:
watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#1 stuck for 26s! [repro:100] RIP: 0010:io_cancel_req_match+0x19/0xa0 io_poll_cancel+0x73/0x170 io_try_cancel+0x7b/0xf0 __io_async_cancel+0x41/0x110
Walk the hash once and cancel every match, as io_cancel_remove() does for futex and waitid. Cancel by user_data only needs its own bucket. __io_async_cancel() still loops until nothing is found, so a request that io-wq parks in the poll hash meanwhile is still cancelled.
A cancel that matches one request now walks the whole hash twice instead of stopping at the match.

item.title: CVE-2026-99797 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
io_uring/cancel: drop sqd->lock while SQPOLL waits
An exiting SQPOLL thread calls io_uring_cancel_generic() with sqd->lock held, and keeps it across cond_resched() and the sleep until nothing is in flight anymore. A zero-copy send notification can't be canceled and stays pending as long as the peer doesn't read, so the lock is held for as long as a user cares to. io_ring_exit_work() needs it to park the thread, and so do IORING_REGISTER_IOWQ_AFF and IOWQ_MAX_WORKERS. With 64 such rings sharing the thread, every iou_exit slot sleeps on the lock and no ring gets freed for anyone.
Drop the lock around cond_resched() and the sleep, like the main loop of the thread does. Each walk of ctx_list is still under one hold, and nothing is kept across the unlock. The thread drops its io-wq, frees its tctx and clears sqd->thread under one hold after the loop, so whoever holds the lock and finds sqd->thread set can still use them.
[axboe: adapted to the schedule_timeout() based loop]

item.title: CVE-2026-99798 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
io_uring: defer foreign io-wq enqueues to task_work
An IOPOLL ring without DEFER_TASKRUN can be reaped by a task other than the one that submitted the I/O. If a polled request is marked REQ_F_REISSUE, io_free_batch_list() calls io_queue_iowq() with the original tctx. Ordinary task exit can tear down tctx->io_wq after draining only the tracked requests. The live request pins the task, but not its io-wq, so the foreign task can race io_wq_put_and_exit() and enqueue through a freed or NULL queue.
Forward foreign userspace enqueues to the owning task before accessing tctx->io_wq. Use a dedicated task_work callback so reissues still go straight to io-wq, and fail them if task_work is running in cancellation mode. Preserve the existing PF_KTHREAD cancellation path. This also covers the other callers of io_queue_iowq() without changing the worker-owned enqueue path.

item.title: CVE-2026-99799 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
io_uring/sqpoll: don't wait for the thread to exit
io_sq_thread_stop() wakes the SQPOLL thread and waits for it to exit. The thread belongs to the thread group that created the ring, so a SIGSTOP or the cgroup freezer holds it in get_signal(), and the wake up doesn't change that. io_ring_exit_work() then sleeps in that wait until someone continues or kills the process. iou_exit has 64 slots, so 64 closed SQPOLL rings of a stopped process keep every other ring from being freed, for everyone.
Don't wait. Set the stop bit, wake the thread, and let it exit when it gets to run again. The sqd can now outlive its last ring, so give it a second refcount with one reference for the rings and one for the thread, and free it with the last one. The thread can't reach a freed ring, rings leave ctx_list before dropping their reference, and the io-wq hash is refcounted.

item.title: CVE-2026-99800 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
io_uring: free the task context after a grace period
A task other than the owner can free a request, io_ring_exit_work() running the local task_work of a DEFER_TASKRUN ring for example, or io_do_iopoll() reaping completions. io_put_task() then takes the else branch:
percpu_counter_sub(&tctx->inflight, 1); if (unlikely(atomic_read(&tctx->in_cancel))) wake_up(&tctx->wait); put_task_struct(tctx->task);
The first line is what lets the owner leave io_uring_cancel_generic(), and on exec it frees the tctx right after. Nothing holds that off for the remaining three lines, the task reference only covers a tctx freed along with the task_struct. It used to work out because io_uring_del_tctx_node() took the uring_lock that the freeing side holds across io_put_task(), until that moved to tctx_lock.
Free the tctx with kfree_rcu(), and enter an RCU read section in io_put_task() before the count is dropped.

item.title: CVE-2026-99801 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
io_uring/bpf-ops: clear bpf_ctx while submitting SQEs
bpf_io_uring_submit_sqes() calls io_submit_sqes() from inside the loop program, with current->bpf_ctx set, and requests issued inline run with it set too. The socket code uses has_current_bpf_ctx() to recognize calls from bpf_setsockopt() and friends, where the caller holds the socket lock and has already been vetted, and skips both.
So a SOCKET_URING_OP_SETSOCKOPT from the SQ passes sockopt_capable() without the capability, and runs without lock_sock(). A task with no capability can set SO_MARK, IP_TRANSPARENT or TCP_REPAIR, and two threads changing IP_OPTIONS on one socket, one through the ring, double free in no time. SOCK_DESTROY via IORING_OP_SENDMSG ends up in tcp_abort() without the lock the same way.
Clear the run context around io_submit_sqes(). The SQEs come from userspace and must be issued like those of any other ring. They still run inside the program's RCU tasks trace read section, so a request that sleeps there holds up that grace period, but other request types do that already.

item.title: CVE-2026-99802 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
io_uring/register: enforce per-task restrictions in io_uring_register_blind()
When io_uring_register(2) is invoked with fd == -1, it dispatches directly to io_uring_register_blind() without checking current->io_uring_restrict.
As a result, a task with per-task register restrictions installed via IORING_REGISTER_RESTRICTIONS can still invoke blind registration opcodes such as IORING_REGISTER_SEND_MSG_RING even when those opcodes are not in the task's allowed register_op bitmap.
Check current->io_uring_restrict->register_op in io_uring_register_blind() before dispatching blind registration opcodes.

item.title: CVE-2026-99803 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
io_uring/net: mask socket type with SOCK_TYPE_MASK in io_socket_bpf_populate()
When an IORING_OP_SOCKET request is prepared in io_socket_prep(), sock->type retains creation flags such as SOCK_CLOEXEC and SOCK_NONBLOCK until __sys_socket_file() masks them off with SOCK_TYPE_MASK during execution.
However, io_socket_bpf_populate() copies sock->type into bctx->socket.type without masking off ~SOCK_TYPE_MASK. As a result, a cBPF filter inspecting bctx->socket.type against socket types such as SOCK_DGRAM or SOCK_STREAM can be bypassed by ORing SOCK_CLOEXEC or SOCK_NONBLOCK into the socket type.
Mask sock->type with SOCK_TYPE_MASK when populating bctx->socket.type.

item.title: CVE-2026-99804 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
io_uring/io-wq: save worker type before dropping its reference
io_wq_cancel_tw_create() inspects cb->func after calling io_worker_cancel_cb(). For an existing worker, that call can drop the last worker reference and wake io_worker_exit(). If the canceling task is preempted, the worker can be unlinked and freed by kfree_rcu() before the callback function is inspected. KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free read in this path.
Save whether the callback belongs to an unpublished continuation worker while its reference is still held, then use the saved result for the conditional free. This preserves the existing accounting and frees only the worker allocated for the canceled continuation.
